candidates.label: Laodicea on the Lycus archaeological site
candidates.support: The extensively excavated site near modern Denizli (Eskihisar), distinct from other ancient cities named Laodicea, is undisputed as the New Testament Laodicea on the Lycus. The coordinate is the Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire's point for the site; Wikidata identifies the same site.

summary.text: Laodicea on the Lycus was a city of the Lycus Valley in Roman Phrygia, grouped with nearby Colossae and Hierapolis in Colossians 4:13. Paul's letter to the Colossians directs that it be read also at Laodicea and that the letter from Laodicea also be read at Colossae, and Laodicea is separately addressed as one of the seven churches of Revelation 2-3, called 'lukewarm' there and rebuked for claiming to 'have need of nothing.'

scripture.textWEB: For I desire to have you know how greatly I struggle for you and for those at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh;
For I testify about him that he has great zeal for you, and for those in Laodicea, and for those in Hierapolis.
Greet the brothers who are in Laodicea, with Nymphas and the assembly that is in his house.
When this letter has been read among you, cause it to be read also in the assembly of the Laodiceans, and that you also read the letter from Laodicea.
saying, “What you see, write in a book and send to the seven assemblies: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and to Laodicea.”
“To the angel of the assembly in Laodicea write: “The Amen, the Faithful and True Witness, the Beginning of God’s creation, says these things:

“I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot. I wish you were cold or hot. So, because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I will vomit you out of my mouth.
